summary: This note outlines the history of Germany during World War I. The German Empire joined the war after its ally Austria-Hungary declared war on Serbia, and it fought the Allies on both the eastern and western fronts. German territory stayed largely safe from invasion apart from East Prussia's brief invasion in 1914, but a Royal Navy blockade caused severe food shortages, especially in the Turnip Winter of 1916-17. Germany's defeat and popular discontent led to the German Revolution of 1918-19, which overthrew the monarchy and established the Weimar Republic.
one_line: Overview of Germany's role in World War I, from its entry as a Central Power through the blockade-driven food crisis to the 1918-19 revolution and the Weimar Republic.
key_facts: The German Empire was one of the Central Powers and lost World War I.
Germany began participating in World War I after its ally Austria-Hungary declared war on Serbia.
German forces fought the Allies on both the eastern and western fronts.
German territory remained relatively safe from widespread invasion for most of the war.
East Prussia was invaded for a brief period in 1914.
A tight blockade imposed by the Royal Navy caused severe food shortages in German cities.
The winter of 1916-17 was known as the Turnip Winter.
The Turnip Winter of 1916-17 was especially severe for food supply in German cities.
Germany's defeat and widespread popular discontent at the end of the war triggered the German Revolution of 1918-19.
The German Revolution of 1918-19 overthrew the monarchy.
The German Revolution of 1918-19 established the Weimar Republic.
